sources.title: Kendujhar district — Gonasika Temple
sources.method: Direct complete relevant body read through web open; not indexed-only.
sources.locator: Description paragraphs and By Road/By Train sections; web lines15–25
sources.excerpt: The shrine of Lord Shiva was constructed by King Laxmi Narayan Bhanja
claims: Hill/valley pilgrimage setting; Brahmeswar Mahadev shrine beside Baitarani.
District sacred account associates the source with Brahma and a cow’s nostrils, then an underground/re-emergent course into Brahma Kunda called Guptaganga.
District attributes construction to King Laxmi Narayan Bhanja during1654–1688; no independent architectural or inscription verification.
Kendujhar is the district page’s road/rail orientation.
limits: Do not present Brahma construction as documented chronology or cow-source imagery as a proven geological mechanism.
Body30km versus road40km conflict; rail40km has a different origin. Omit precise distance and timing.
Claim Bhubaneswar is only civil airport in state is stale; omit.
No present service availability, opening hours, fees, steps, visitor permissions, bathing safety or best-month guidance.
Omit exotic flora/fauna and community-as-attraction language.

sources.title: Kendujhar district — Culture & Heritage
sources.method: Direct web original; bounded Baruni Jatra and Sivaratri sections read.
sources.excerpt: the jatra is held at Gonasika near Brahmeswar Mahadev Temple
claims: District associates Baruni Jatra with Gonasika/Brahmeswar shrine and ritual bathing at Brahma Kunda.
District also names Gonasika in its Sivaratri account.
limits: No current festival date/calendar or attendance verified.
Omit undated crowd estimate, access characterization and stereotypes.
A ritual-bathing description is not a safety recommendation or water-quality assessment.
